correctness.rationale: For n,d>=2 over C and N=binom(n+d-1,d), choose diagonal one-parameter subgroup with weights 1,B,...,B^(n-1), B>d. Degree-d monomial weights are pairwise distinct by base-B representation, so ambient P^{N-1} fixed locus consists of N coordinate monomials. Every monomial defines a singular projective hypersurface except xy for (n,d)=(2,2): a pure power is nonreduced, and for n>=3 distinct coordinate components meet; binary reduced monomial xy exists only at d=2. Thus the smooth coefficient-space U fixed locus is empty except one point for binary quadrics. Algebraic C* Euler localization gives chi_c(U)=0 or 1 respectively, and additivity gives chi(D)=N or 2. The independent checker verified 2969 monomial cases with exact weight distinctness; infinite proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The discriminant is a fundamental projective parameter-space boundary. A uniform characteristic across all dimensions and degrees, plus the exceptional pair and compactly-supported complement vanishing, is a reusable exact invariant distinguishing coefficient spaces from moduli quotients. The fixed-locus classification is object-dependent, not a generic numerical recomputation.
